$meta.name: JRK Analytics Design Tokens
$meta.description: Single source of truth. Run `npm run build` to regenerate dist/. Never hand-edit dist/.
$meta.$surfaceNote: The CARD is the chart surface, not the page. The page plane is white and cards are a soft gray-purple, so every chart mark is measured against #f5f5fa.
$meta.validated: Categorical palette passes dataviz six-checks in both modes against the surfaces above. Run `npm run validate` after any color change.

ramp.$comment: Raw hue ramps. Semantic tokens below reference these by name; components never reference a ramp directly.

neutral.$comment: Two-sided by design. The LIGHT half carries a violet cast so the tinted cards and the ink read as one family. The DARK half (700 and below) is achromatic — a black page with neutral shadow-grey tiles, which keeps the indigo accent and the chart hues as the only color in the dark UI.

color.$comment: Semantic color tokens. Every entry has a light and dark value; dark is SELECTED for the dark surface, never an automatic flip.

surface.$comment: Light mode is INVERTED from a conventional dashboard: white page plane, cards carrying a soft gray-purple tint, popovers white so they still lift. Dark mode keeps the same LAYERING but goes achromatic — a true black page with neutral shadow-grey tiles. In both modes the card, not the page, is the chart surface.

banner.use: sheet title bar and section bands — the one heavy element in a dense report

text.$comment: Validated against BOTH the page plane and the card. In light mode the card is the darker of the two; in dark mode the black page is the darker, so the grey card is the binding case there. Dark ink is neutral grey — a violet-tinted ink on neutral tiles reads as a color cast rather than as a choice.

disabled.use: disabled label — decorative only, never load-bearing

inverse.use: text on inverse surface / solid accent

border.$comment: Deliberately near-invisible. Cards separate from the page by their FILL, not by a rule; these are for inputs, table hairlines, and chart chrome. Neutral in dark to match the achromatic tiles.

accent.$comment: Periwinkle-leaning indigo. Solid fill uses indigo-600 — indigo-500 measures only 4.0:1 with white text, under AA.

wash.use: selected row tint, soft badge fill

status.$comment: Reserved meanings. Never reused as a chart series color. Always shipped with an icon + label — never color alone. `mark` is for fills/dots (3:1 target); `text` is the AA-4.5:1 text step; `wash` is the soft badge fill.

ring.use: 2px focus ring — must clear 3:1 on the page, the card, AND the inset well

offset.use: ring offset, so the ring reads on any surface

chart.$comment: Data-viz layer. Categorical order is the CVD-safety mechanism — assign slots 1..N in order, NEVER cycle. A 9th series folds into 'Other' or facets. Scatter/bubble/choropleth/small-multiples cap at 3 series (all-pairs validated).

categorical.$softening: Softened as far as the gates allow: lightness lifted and chroma cut ~24% from the saturated originals, holding each hue and — critically — holding the LIGHTNESS SPREAD. Protan/deutan viewers separate colors mostly by lightness, so flattening the spread to make everything uniformly pale is exactly what collapses CVD separation. Light and dark were tuned independently (light band 0.43-0.77 is wider than dark 0.48-0.67). Going further fails: light hits the adjacent-CVD floor, dark hits the top of its lightness band.

reliefRequired.note: Sub-3:1 on the light card surface. Ship visible direct labels or the table view when these are used as fills. Not dismissable. Softening moved a fourth hue into this list — the cost of the softer look.

tint.$comment: Pastel fills for LARGE marks whose identity is already carried by something else — an axis category label, a direct value label, or a legend with numbers beside it. This is the set that produces the soft reference look. It is deliberately NOT a categorical palette: these sit far above the lightness band and below the chroma floor, so they cannot do identity work and the validator does not check them for CVD separation. Using a tint where color IS the identity channel is a bug. Pair with `chart.tintInk` for any label set inside the fill.
tint.rule: legal only when the mark is axis-labeled, direct-labeled, or accompanied by a value in the legend

ink.use: label set inside a tint fill

ordinalFloor.note: Ordinal ramps must clear 2:1 vs surface — do not go lighter (light) or darker (dark) than these. The tinted card surface is darker than white, so the light floor sits a step deeper than it would on a white page.

diverging.note: Two hues + a NEUTRAL gray midpoint. Equal step count per arm. Never a hue at the midpoint, never a rainbow.

chrome.$comment: surface is the CARD, not the page — that is what chart marks sit on and what the validator measures against.

family.mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

radius.$comment: Deliberately generous — this is the main lever for the softer, curvier feel. dataEnd is the exception and stays small on purpose: a heavily rounded bar tip makes the exact endpoint ambiguous, and the bar's whole job is to be read against the axis. 6px on a 16px bar is already the practical ceiling.

shadow.$comment: Dark mode leans almost entirely on the lightened surface, not the shadow: against a true black page a drop shadow is invisible, so the grey tile IS the elevation cue. The dark shadows here only tighten the edge.

size.$comment: Control heights and layout rails. Carried over from jrk_agents where they were already established.

sheet.$comment: Spreadsheet density. Deliberately tighter than the rest of the library — a financial report's job is to get a year of months on one screen, and the app's own row heights would make that impossible. Fixed track widths, because the Excel-style column bar can only line up with the data if every row shares one track list.
sheet.label: 104px

motion.$comment: All transitions must be wrapped in a prefers-reduced-motion guard — handled in base.css.
